stem: When procuring third-party commercial software, how should an enterprise verify a vendor's accessibility claims?

options.text: By obtaining a current ACR/VPAT and relying on the vendor's contractual warranty of conformance.
options.rationale: An ACR/VPAT plus a warranty does not verify the accuracy of the vendor's claims or the product's actual conformance.

options.text: By requiring the vendor to complete a security and accessibility questionnaire and attest to the final results.
options.rationale: Questionnaires and self-attestations are vendor assertions, not independent evidence of accessibility.

options.text: By commissioning a third-party audit of the vendor's development process rather than the delivered product.
options.shortLabel: Process audit instead of product testing
options.rationale: A process audit can miss product-level barriers; verification must test the delivered interface with assistive technology.

options.text: By reviewing the ACR/VPAT, testing the product independently, and making accessibility commitments contractual.
options.shortLabel: Reviewing ACR/VPAT, testing, and contractual terms
options.rationale: Thorough procurement verification requires critically analyzing the ACR/VPAT for accuracy, conducting independent manual and assistive technology testing, and securing binding contractual terms for ongoing remediation.

explanation: Procuring accessible third-party Information and Communication Technology (ICT) requires robust due diligence rather than accepting claims at face value. Organizations should: (1) Request and scrutinize a detailed Accessibility Conformance Report (ACR)—generated using the Voluntary Product Accessibility Template (VPAT)—paying close attention to detailed remarks; (2) Conduct independent validation testing using automated tools, keyboard navigation, and assistive technologies; and (3) Integrate explicit accessibility requirements, defect remediation timelines, and warranties into the final vendor contract.

references.title: US General Services Administration: Requesting Accessibility Conformance Reports
